note: Normative requirements for downstream authorizers and policy lifecycle verifiers. This repository contains no such runtime: its tests validate declaration shape and this fixture container, not execution of these decisions. given/expect are semantic test notation, not wire fields or new decision enums. All other applicable authorization and governance checks pass unless a vector states otherwise. Time values are comparable trusted instants in seconds. An emergency declaration alone is never an approval or activation.

vectors.reason: A proof is expired when now >= expiration, including the boundary instant.
An existing session or cached allow decision cannot extend the proof's validity.

expect.requiredTransition: predeclared safe pause or independently authorized containment

vectors.reason: Starting before expiration does not authorize later privileged effects. The safe transition cannot manufacture further ordinary authority.
Run once for each symbolic malformed expiration case; an unprovable validity interval cannot authorize execution.
A verifier that cannot establish validity time cannot treat proofs or emergency activations as unexpired.
A calculation failure cannot substitute a less restrictive value or increase capacity.
Missing standing is not evidence of full standing and cannot authorize ordinary execution.
An outage or emergency label grants no separate capability.
A valid independent capability permits evaluation of its exact action, subject to local capacity, Soul, limits, logging, and every remaining check. It does not revive expired ordinary authority.
The same-candidate A > E veto survives emergency activation and human approval.
Run once for each Soul result; emergency authority cannot bypass sovereignty checks.
Administrator access cannot replace the independent custody threshold.
Forwarding, wrapping, or caching cannot refresh proof evidence or extend its original authorization lifetime.
An outage cannot lower the ordinary proof verification quorum. Separate emergency approval is not an Oracle quorum substitute.
An incident cannot waive advance notice, independent review, ratification, or preinstallation requirements to introduce new authority.

Run once per candidate case. A proposed replacement or first-installation roster cannot appoint its own approving electorate; another policy ID cannot evade incumbent governance. Stricter incumbent and candidate conditions remain applicable.
Changing approved payload bytes without a properly approved successor cannot preserve the policy identity or activation validity.
A consumed incident-bound activation cannot be replayed as fresh authority.
Valid historical signatures do not authorize rollback past the durable approved policy state.
Revocation overrides an otherwise unexpired activation.
Emergency effects require a durable receipt before execution, including during a logging outage.
Continuing outage conditions cannot automatically renew an emergency activation.
The incident deadline is first activation issuance plus the approved duration. Fresh activations, pauses, process restarts, or renamed incident identifiers cannot reset or extend that deadline.
Reactivation and restarts cannot replenish an action's execution budget within the incident.
Run once per mismatch; an emergency action is an exact enumeration, with no wildcard, alias expansion, parameter extension, or unapproved local evaluation profile substitution.

Run once per failure case. Signatures on claimed dates do not prove elapsed review; trusted history, fixed proposal bytes, minimum periods, external review, and resolution of required objections remain mandatory.
A proof cannot authorize before issuance, even when its declared lifetime is within ten seconds and its expiration is in the future.

expect.requiredTransition: previously declared bounded safe transition with its own authorization

vectors.reason: Run once per loss case. Emergency limits and evidence requirements apply throughout execution, including the four-hour maximum when reached. Starting earlier does not authorize completing the original task after a required condition is lost.

given.deploymentCases: every conformance level and every zone color

vectors.reason: Run each expiration case at every supported conformance level and zone color. A lifetime above ten seconds is invalid even while now is between issuance and expiration; the former 30- or 60-second allowances cannot extend ordinary authority.

Run once per binding case. Trusted Level 3 requires SHA-384 for every emergency binding under KTP-CRYPTO. A syntactically valid SHA-256 declaration or candidate-selected lower level cannot override the trusted requirement; the declaration checker alone has no trusted level context.
